text:
The evidence can't tell us whether clearing is happening today. It covers only 2021, and the latest year in the data series is 2025.

For 2021, Hansen/UMD mapped about 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss, or 2.23% of the 3,643.5 ha property. A later year was observed and the JRC 2020 forest reference agrees on 98% of the affected area, so the loss is well corroborated.

Most of that loss (68.1 ha) falls on planted pine (*Pinus elliottii* and *Pinus taeda*). None is native forest, and 13.2 ha lies outside mapped forest. That pattern is consistent with plantation harvesting, but the evidence doesn't establish the cause. It also doesn't show whether this was deforestation or land-use change, whether it was legal, who was responsible, or any compliance status.

To answer your question, you would need loss data for 2022 onward, or recent imagery or alerts.
